name: Pietro Pileo di Prata
summary:
Pietro Pileo di Prata (c.1330–1400) was an Italian bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the affairs of his times, particularly in the conclave that led to the election of Pope Boniface IX. Di Prata's diplomatic prowess earned him the nickname 'cardinal with three hats', which he obtained successively from Urban VI, Clement VII, and Boniface IX.

As a key figure in the papal conclave of 1389–1390, di Prata's influence extended beyond Italy, shaping the course of European politics during a time of great turmoil. His negotiations with foreign leaders, including King John I of Portugal, demonstrate his ability to navigate complex international relationships.

Despite his significant diplomatic achievements, di Prata's legacy is also marked by controversy. His role in the conclave that led to Pope Boniface IX's election has been subject to interpretation and debate among historians.

In the annals of history, Pietro Pileo di Prata's name stands as a testament to the enduring power of diplomacy and the complexities of medieval politics.
